correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly constructs all invariant spectral blocks and verifies their dimensions total \(2p+q\). Convex averaging gives the true global infimum. In four parameter ranges, eigenvalue inequalities and holding budgets furnish matching universal lower bounds. Equality and feasibility give the entire interval of optimal intra-equal-parts weights. Exact rational 2,478 tests, 257 separate LP solves, 52 assembled full-matrix eigenproblems and 40 transition tests corroborate, but do not substitute for, the analytical infinite-family argument. Since orbit averages of nonnegative edge weights are zero only when all such entries are zero, the asserted global edge-deletion threshold follows for unrestricted optimizers.

originality.rationale: Original contribution is a complete parametric solution, with sharp ratios 1/2, 1, 2, and 4 and full intervals of optimal edge probabilities, for the imbalanced graph \(K_{p,p,q}\). Boyd et al. (2009) provide the relevant general multipartite block decomposition, but only explicitly solve the bipartite case in their Section 5.4.2; a new sharp two-weight minimax analysis is needed. The equal-sized cycle multipartite case in Jafarizadeh (2010) does not settle p unequal q. Originality is a best-knowledge conclusion, with unindexed-literature risk.

value.rationale: Complete tripartite networks with two equally sized classes are a natural step beyond the known bipartite and balanced cases. The exact finite-size solution reveals nontrivial and sharp ratios \(q/p=1/2,1,2,4\), and shows the onset of optional and then mandatory elimination of an entire edge orbit. Characterizing all invariant optimizers, not just a single optimal SLEM, provides a structural benchmark for symmetric stochastic weight design. In fact, beyond the last threshold the optimal removal of the A–B edge orbit is mandatory even without symmetry assumptions.
